text:
maria: heads up — after yesterday's prefill-affinity tweak we saw a 6–12ms p95 jump on small-chat workloads starting ~03:10 UTC. correlated with reduced throughput on some pods.
aj: saw that in dashboards too. looks like latency jump coincides with kernel selection flipping to kernel_v2_slow for many short sequences.
noah: can you paste the probe/sample trace?
maria: pasted a trimmed trace below (from perf-trace):
```
REQUEST id=aa12 seq_len=45
queue_wait=2.1ms prefill_wait=0.9ms kernel=kernel_v2_slow run=7.4ms kv_hit=false
KV lookup: cold miss, fallback to host memory
```
aj: kv_hit=false is interesting — prefill-affinity was supposed to increase prefix reuse and KV hits.
ryan: my hunch: prefill window growth caused microbatches to coalesce into shapes that the kernel selector mapped poorly — picks slower path because of padding/shape distribution.
sekhar: I pushed a quick flamegraph of the GPU kernels and host copy times — see gist: https://redwood/gist/zz123 (summary: memcpy host->device spiked, kernel times up 20%).
aj: do we have batch shape histograms before/after rollout?
maria: attaching quick counts: pre-rollout most requests were shape {1x64,1x128}, post-rollout we got more {4x32} coalesced. selector maps {4x32} -> kernel_v2_slow due to presumed kv-memory layout.
noah: that explains both kernel change and KV misses — our KV cache lookup index assumes per-request layout; coalesced batches are causing misaligned KV indices.
ryan: can we reproduce locally with the replay harness? i'll try to force the new prefill config and run 1k traces.
aj: also check token_budget target — if the budget increased, we might be waiting longer to form batches which changes shapes.
maria: token_budget was bumped from 40 -> 80 tokens in the rollout. i can roll it back to 40 on a couple of canary pools.
sekhar: quick test idea: revert only token_budget to see if kernel selection reverts. if so, root cause narrow to budget/shape.
noah: repro attempt: ran replay with token_budget=80 — reproduced kernel flip + host memcpy spike. set token_budget=40 — kernel selector preferred kernel_v1_fast and memcpy drops.
ryan: great, looks like token_budget change is the trigger, not prefill affinity alone.
aj: what's the risk of reverting token_budget cluster-wide? do we lose batching efficiency for long sequences?
maria: long sequences throughput will drop ~3% in my bench but short-seq p95 improves ~10ms. customer-impact tradeoff seems worth immediate rollback for stability.
devops-bot: deploy pipeline: rolling-revert-token-budget starting job #4821 (canary pools: c-pool-3, c-pool-5). ETA ~8m.
ryan: while rollback runs, can we create a selector rule: if batch_shapes hist has >60% coalesced small-shapes, prefer kernel_v1_fast override.
sekhar: possible — quick rule implemented in selector config language. but it's a band-aid; we should fix KV layout assumptions for coalesced batches.
noah: i'll open an infra task to audit KV index mapping for coalesced batches and add unit tests for shape permutations.
aj: add perf regression test to CI that runs mixed short/long traces across token_budget values.
maria: thanks. action items: 1) rollback token_budget on canaries (in progress), 2) add selector override rule (ryan), 3) infra task for KV mapping (noah), 4) CI perf test (aj).
ryan: will also instrument a thin metric: kernel_selector_reason per-batch to make root-cause faster next time.
sekhar: logging note: make sure not to log full KV keys (PII) when we dump indices. mask them.
maria: agreed. i'll follow up with a short postmortem after we confirm rollback results.
aj: nice triage team — quick and data-driven. :thumbsup:
devops-bot: deploy #4821 succeeded on canary pools at 2104567938.
maria: canaries look good so far — p95 dropped back ~9ms. rolling revert scheduled for all pools in 30m unless objections.
ryan: no objections from me. proceeding with selector rule PR in parallel.
noah: PR refs: KV-314 audit + tests, will link once created.
sekhar: add a note to run end-to-end evals (latency+throughput) after full rollback.
maria: will coordinate and publish results here. thanks everyone.
